name: Great North Road
wiki: Great North Road, New South Wales
note: Linear heritage feature: the convict-built Great North Road, a UNESCO Australian Convict Sites listing; visitors walk or drive sections of it (Old Great North Road walk in Dharug NP). Long linear feature, so place at its visitor access point.

name: Somersby Falls
note: Waterfall: three-tier falls in Somersby, a short walk down a valley; free picnic area, car park fee. Named by Wikivoyage and the Brisbane Water NP walking track list.

name: Wondabyne
note: Railway station (Wondabyne) on the Central Coast line with no road access, reached only by train or walking track; Wikivoyage calls it famed for remoteness. Visitors get off to walk to Patonga.

name: Woy Woy
note: Town: bayside commuter town on Brisbane Water, named as a holiday destination by Wikivoyage.

name: Tascott
note: Suburb: quiet waterfront suburb on Brisbane Water beside the national park; named by Wikivoyage as a place of interest, no specific sight.

name: Edogawa Commemorative Garden
note: Japanese garden in East Gosford, a gift from sister city Edogawa; free entry, koi feeding, open daily 9:30AM-4PM.

name: Gosford Regional Gallery
note: Regional art gallery in East Gosford with rotating local and international exhibitions; free entry.

name: Pelican Feeding
note: Daily pelican feeding platform at The Entrance, where the town calls itself the Pelican Capital of Australia; permanent daily activity.

name: The Skillion
note: Coastal lookout and short walk over cliffs and the Terrigal Formation rock, above Terrigal; Wikivoyage calls it hikeable with gorgeous views.

name: Central Coast Marine Discovery Centre
note: Marine science museum with interactive exhibits at Terrigal, paid entry (child/concession $7, adult $10), open daily 10AM-4PM.

name: Australian Reptile Park
note: Wildlife park in Somersby with crocodile and bird shows and unfenced kangaroos, emus and wombats; paid entry; a permanent visitor attraction.

name: Australian Rainforest Sanctuary at the Forest of Tranquility
note: Rainforest sanctuary with walks and wallabies on the Central Coast, paid entry ($12 adult per Wikivoyage); a permanent visitor site.

name: Glenworth Valley Outdoor Adventures
note: Operator: outdoor activity company at Peats Ridge (horse riding, kayaking, quad biking, abseiling). Operator, not a place.

name: Wamberal Beach
note: Surf beach at Wamberal, which Wikivoyage considers one of the best on the NSW east coast.

name: Forresters Beach
note: Beach at Northavon/Forresters Beach with clear water and a view; Wikivoyage names it for its water clarity and the adjoining national park.

name: Terrigal Beach
note: Beach: 4 km unbroken surf beach at Terrigal with a rock pool at the southern end, surrounded by cafes.

name: Central Coast Stadium
note: Sports venue at Gosford (Industree Group Stadium) for Central Coast Mariners A-League matches; only matches Oct-May, so a venue for events rather than a permanent attraction.

name: Central Coast Reef and Game Fishing Charters
note: Operator: reef and game fishing charters from Fishermans Beach, The Haven.

name: Bouddi National Park
note: National park: coastal cliffs, beaches, walks and lookouts near Killcare, one of Australia's first marine protected areas (NSW NPWS).

name: Brisbane Water National Park
note: National park: bushwalks, cycle trails, wildflowers and Aboriginal engraving sites around Brisbane Water (NSW NPWS).

name: Dharug National Park
note: National park near Wisemans Ferry (Hawkesbury/Central Coast edge) with the Old Great North Road World Heritage walk and canoeing (NSW NPWS).

name: Wyrrabalong National Park
note: National park beside The Entrance: beaches, the last coastal rainforest on the Central Coast, and whale watching (NSW NPWS).

name: Watagans National Park
note: National park in the Watagan Mountains west of Wyong/Lake Macquarie: rainforest walks and lookouts; no NPWS page fetched, visitor source not confirmed.

name: Yengo National Park
note: National park of Aboriginal significance around Mount Yengo; remote with limited visitor access, no visitor page fetched.

name: Mount Yengo
note: Mountain of Aboriginal significance above the Wollombi Valley; Wikivoyage lists it as a place to see, with no formal visitor track.

name: Wollombi
note: Historic village in the Wollombi Valley with heritage buildings (St John's Anglican Church, former courthouse, general store), the Convict Trail and Koolang Observatory.

name: Wisemans Ferry
note: Village and river-crossing ferry on the Hawkesbury, the gateway to Dharug National Park; the ferry is a vehicle, the village is the place.

name: Patonga
note: Village on Brisbane Water: fish and chips and beach view, end of the Patonga to Pearl Beach walk (NSW NPWS).

name: Umina Beach
note: Beach and town on Brisbane Water; NPWS directs visitors there for lunch and picnic supplies before the park.

name: Pearl Beach
note: Village and beach at the end of the Patonga to Pearl Beach walking track, Brisbane Water NP.

name: Great North Walk
note: Long-distance walk (about 250 km, Sydney to Newcastle) with stages 9 and 10 through Brisbane Water NP; a long trail.

name: Mooney Mooney Nature Walk
note: Short nature walk in Brisbane Water NP, listed by NPWS.

name: Patonga to Pearl Beach Walking Track
note: Walking track between Patonga and Pearl Beach, Brisbane Water NP, listed by NPWS.

name: Wondabyne to Patonga Walking Track
note: Walking track between Wondabyne station and Patonga, Brisbane Water NP, listed by NPWS.

name: Bulgandry Art Site
note: Aboriginal Place with rock engravings in Brisbane Water NP; NPWS guided tours; ancient art site.

name: Bouddi Coastal Walk
note: Coastal walking track through Bouddi NP between Killcare and Maitland Bay; the park's main walk.

name: Maitland Bay
note: Beach in Bouddi NP with the Maitland Bay Information Centre and a walking track; NPWS listing.

name: Putty Beach
note: Beach with campground at Bouddi NP, named by NPWS for camping and swimming.

name: Tallow Beach
note: Beach with campground in Bouddi NP near Killcare, named by NPWS for camping and swimming.

name: Little Beach (Bouddi)
note: Beach with campground in Bouddi NP (named by NPWS); disambiguated by park because the name is shared.

name: Allen Strom Lookout
note: Lookout over Bouddi NP at Killcare, reached by Wards Hill Road; Wikivoyage lists it as a stop.

name: Bullimah Lookout
note: Lookout at the southern end of the Bullimah Spur track in Bouddi NP.

name: Gerrin Point Lookout
note: Coastal lookout on the Bouddi Coastal Walk, Bouddi NP.

name: Marie Byles Lookout
note: Lookout on The Scenic Road, Killcare Heights, Bouddi NP.

name: Mount Bouddi Walking Track
note: Walking track to Mount Bouddi (Dingeldei) in Bouddi NP, listed by Wikivoyage.

name: Lake Macquarie
note: Lake: the largest saltwater lake in NSW (Lake Macquarie), with beaches, fishing, sailing and Swansea Channel; a lake destination (Wikivoyage Lake Macquarie).

name: Caves Beach
note: Beach at Caves Beach where natural sea caves can be walked at low tide (Wikivoyage Swansea).

name: Catherine Hill Bay
wiki: Catherine Hill Bay, New South Wales
coordinates_source: wikipedia:Catherine Hill Bay, New South Wales
note: Beach and village at Catherine Hill Bay on the Lake Macquarie coast, named by Wikivoyage Swansea as a beach to visit.

name: Redhead Beach
note: Surf beach at Redhead on the Lake Macquarie coast, named by Wikivoyage Swansea.

name: Blacksmiths Beach
note: Beach at Blacksmiths on the Lake Macquarie coast, named by Wikivoyage Swansea.

name: Swansea Channel
note: Channel with a famous fishing spot under the Swansea bridge (kingfish), per Wikivoyage Swansea.

name: South Sea Islands Museum
note: Museum of South Sea Islands artefacts and cultural items at Cooranbong (Avondale University), open Wed/Sat/Sun 2-4PM.

name: Lake Macquarie Variety Playground
note: Playground: a 2-hectare play space in Speers Point Park with maze, play boat and bike circuit. A local playground; Wikivoyage lists it under Do.

name: Strike Charlestown
note: Venue: bowling alley, laser tag and karaoke at Charlestown Square. Commercial venue, not a visitor attraction.

name: Richmond Vale Railway Museum
note: Museum: heritage railway museum at Richmond Vale near Cessnock; OSM and Wikipedia only, no visitor-agency or guide listing fetched.

name: Christ Church Cathedral
note: Cathedral on Church Street, Newcastle; tours of the interior and the tower with a guided map (paid). (Scorer matched a same-name spot in Nelson, NZ; that is a different place, so not counted as existing.)

name: Nobbys Head
note: Headland and pier (convict-built, 1846) with a vantage point over the harbour and Nobbys Beach; open to pedestrians.

name: Newcastle Museum
note: Museum in three historic railway workshops at Workshop Way, with exhibits on local history, BHP steelworks and coal mining; Tue-Sun 10AM-5PM.

name: Fort Scratchley
note: Historic fort and military museum on Nobbys Road with guided tunnel tours; fired on by a Japanese submarine in 1942.

name: The Lock-Up Cultural Centre
note: Cultural centre in a former police lock-up on Hunter Street: police museum and John Paynter Gallery; gold coin entry.

name: Newcastle Art Gallery
note: Art gallery on Laman Street with a collection of Australian art and travelling shows; free entry (Tue-Sun 10AM-5PM).

name: Miss Porter's House
note: Edwardian terrace house museum on King Street, open only one afternoon a month (National Trust).

name: Newcastle Foreshore
note: Harbour foreshore parkland, bars and cafes on old marshalling yards, with a playground and live music at Queens Wharf.

name: King Edward Park
note: Clifftop park above the Bogey Hole with picnic and barbecue areas and ocean views (Wikivoyage Newcastle). Wikipedia title is a disambiguation page with no Newcastle article; views 0.

name: Mount Sugarloaf Lookout
note: Lookout at West Wallsend over the Hunter Valley and Newcastle region.

name: ANZAC Walk
note: Clifftop walking bridge and ridgeline path from Strzelecki Lookout at The Hill to Bar Beach, honouring WWI ANZACs; free.

name: Hunter Wetlands Centre
note: Wetlands centre at Sandgate with 45 ha of walking, cycling and canoe trails, birdlife and picnic areas; open 9AM-5PM.

name: Blackbutt Reserve
note: 182 ha bushland reserve with wildlife exhibits, walking trails and a flying fox colony; Wikivoyage and Visit Newcastle name it.

name: Fernleigh Track
note: 15.5 km shared cycle and walking path on a former railway from Adamstown to Belmont; Wikivoyage names it.

name: Newcastle Regional Library
note: Civic library on Laman Street (war memorial building), listed by Wikivoyage; a library and civic building, not a visit stop in itself.

name: Bar Beach
note: Surf beach at The Hill, Newcastle, regarded by Wikivoyage as the best of the city beaches; surfing and kitesurfing.

name: Nobbys Beach
note: Beach beside Nobbys Head and Newcastle station, one of the safer swimming beaches in the city.

name: Newcastle Beach
note: City-centre beach next to the CBD and the harbour foreshore.

name: Newcastle Ocean Baths
note: Historic ocean baths opened 1922 close to the city centre, with the Grandstand for sunbathing; open in winter too.

name: Merewether Ocean Baths
note: Ocean baths complex at Merewether, described by Wikivoyage as the largest in the southern hemisphere; free.

name: The Bogey Hole
note: Convict-carved rock ocean pool at the foot of King Edward Park, Newcastle.

name: Soldiers Baths
note: Rock ocean pool on the Bathers Way, Newcastle, named by Visit Newcastle in its offbeat list.

name: Bathers Way
note: Coastal walking path linking Newcastle's beaches, baths and headlands, listed by Visit Newcastle.

name: Hunter Valley Gardens
note: Australia's largest display garden at Broke Road, Pokolbin; paid entry; daily 9AM-5PM.

name: Pokolbin
note: Village at the heart of Hunter Valley wine country: the cellar doors and vineyards cluster around it (Wikivoyage Pokolbin).

name: Tyrrell's
note: Winery cellar door in Pokolbin; Wikivoyage names it only as host of the Jazz in the Vines event. Venue: a cellar door, a tasting business, judge against the venue-only rule.

name: Wyndham Estate
note: Winery cellar door at Dalwood, one of the Hunter's oldest wineries; OSM attraction and Wikipedia only.

name: Lindeman's
note: Winery brand with a Hunter Valley cellar door; Wikipedia only. Venue: winery and tasting room.

name: Hot-air Ballooning Hunter Valley
note: Operator: hot-air balloon flights over the Hunter Valley (Lovedale); operator, not a place.

name: Gone Walkabout Safaris
note: Operator: winery tour company picking up from Newcastle and Hunter Valley accommodation; operator, not a place.

name: Boutique Wine Tours
note: Operator: luxury day tours of Hunter Valley wineries from Sydney; operator, not a place.

name: Aussie Wine Tours
note: Operator: Cessnock-based winery tour company; operator, not a place.

name: Cessnock
note: Town: wine-country service town with historic buildings and a heritage walking-tour brochure; base for the vineyards (Wikivoyage Cessnock).

name: Cessnock Heritage Walk
note: Self-guided heritage walk of Cessnock's buildings from 1900 to WWII, per Wikivoyage; a district walk, not one site.

name: Mount Royal National Park
note: National park in the Gondwana Rainforests World Heritage area, named by Wikivoyage Hunter Valley natural attractions.

name: Werakata National Park
note: National park in the Lower Hunter near Cessnock: birdwatching, cycle loops and picnic at Astills (NSW NPWS).

name: Hunter Valley Wildlife Park
note: Wildlife park: animal park in the Hunter (Beresfield/Thornton area), paid entry; Wikipedia only, no visitor agency listing fetched.

name: Maitland
note: City: historic city on the Hunter River with heritage buildings, art gallery and Maitland Gaol; Wikivoyage Maitland.

name: Maitland Gaol
note: Historic sandstone prison at East Maitland open to visitors, 9AM-4PM; paid; Wikivoyage calls it very freaky.

name: Maitland Regional Art Gallery
note: Regional art gallery on High Street, Maitland; closed Mondays.

name: Cintra House
note: Heritage-listed late 19th-century residence and former private hospital on Regent Street; listed by Wikivoyage, public access not confirmed (likely exterior only).

name: Walka Water Works
note: Heritage 1880s water works at Oakhampton Heights with a pumphouse, grounds and picnic area; open to visitors on set times.

name: Buttai Barn
note: Barn at Buttai, 20 minutes from Maitland, for traditional bush dancing; 9AM-5PM per Wikivoyage.

name: Maitland Park
note: Sports park in Maitland with playground, netball, cricket, bowling club and aquatic centre; a local ordinary park.

name: Morpeth
note: Historic village on the Hunter River outside Maitland with cafes and boutique shops, open Thursday to Sunday (Wikivoyage Maitland).

name: Morpeth Jazz Festival
note: Annual New Orleans-style jazz festival in September in Morpeth. Event, not a permanent spot.

name: Bitter & Twisted Boutique Beer Festival
note: Annual beer and music festival at East Maitland. Event, not a permanent spot.

name: Hunter Valley Steamfest
note: Annual steam-train festival in the Maitland Railway Station precinct. Event, not a permanent spot.

name: Dungog
note: Country town in the Dungog Shire, gateway to Barrington Tops and Chichester; Wikivoyage Dungog.

name: Dungog Museum
note: Local history museum on Dowling Street, Dungog; Wed and Sat afternoons.

name: Barrington Tops National Park
note: World Heritage Gondwana rainforest national park rising to over 1500 m: walking tracks, camping, picnic areas and lookouts (NSW NPWS).

name: Careys Peak
note: Peak in Barrington Tops NP with a walking track and views (NSW NPWS track list).

name: Devils Hole Lookout
note: Lookout and picnic area in Barrington Tops NP (NSW NPWS track list).

name: Gloucester Falls
note: Waterfall in Barrington Tops NP with a picnic area and walking track (NSW NPWS track list).

name: Gloucester Tops
note: Plateau area of Barrington Tops NP named in NPWS track list; redirects to the park article, so views are the park's.

name: Mount Allyn
note: Peak in the Barrington Tops area; OSM and Wikipedia only, no visitor track named.

name: Brumlow Top
note: Peak in Barrington Tops area; OSM and Wikipedia only, no visitor track named.

name: Stockton Beach
note: Beach and sand dune system, the largest moving coastal sand dune in the southern hemisphere; 4WD, camel and sandboarding tours from Birubi (Wikivoyage Port Stephens).

name: Port Stephens
note: Bay and region: whale and dolphin watching, sand dunes and Tomaree National Park; a region-level name, not a single place. Wikipedia title is the bay article.

name: One Mile Beach
note: Beach on Port Stephens: surfing and atmospheric views down the peninsula; named by Wikivoyage. Wikipedia article is the town of One Mile, so views are the town's.

name: Mount Tomaree
note: Summit in Tomaree NP: 2.2 km return walk to panoramic views over Port Stephens and the islands (Wikivoyage; NSW NPWS Tomaree Head Summit walk).

name: Gan Gan Lookout
note: Lookout on Lily Hill Road above Nelson Bay with views of the bay region (Wikivoyage Port Stephens).

name: Point Stephens Lighthouse
note: Lighthouse on Fingal Island, reached by Fingal Spit at low tide or by boat or kayak; NPWS runs a Fingal Island eco-walk and lighthouse tour.

name: Shark Island (Port Stephens)
note: Island in Port Stephens with unspoilt beaches, reached at low tide via Shark Beach (Wikivoyage Port Stephens).

name: Tomaree National Park
note: National park on the Port Stephens headlands: 27 km coastal walk, whale watching lookouts, Fort Tomaree and beaches (NSW NPWS).

name: Tomaree Head Summit Walk
coordinates_source: osm/wikivoyage: Mount Tomaree summit point (same summit)
note: Steep short summit walk in Tomaree NP with panoramic ocean views (NSW NPWS).

name: Tomaree Coastal Walk
note: 27 km connected coastal walking track through Tomaree NP (NSW NPWS).

name: Fort Tomaree
note: World War II gun emplacements on Tomaree Head in Tomaree NP (NSW NPWS).

name: Birubi Point Aboriginal Place
note: Aboriginal Place at Birubi Point, Tomaree NP, with a storytelling and walking-tour program (NSW NPWS).

name: Birubi Point to One Mile Beach Walking Track
note: Walking track between Birubi Point and One Mile Beach, Tomaree NP (NSW NPWS).

name: Shoal Bay
note: Bay and village in Port Stephens on the Tomaree coast: beach, swimming and the Shoal Bay to Fingal Bay walk (NSW NPWS).

name: Fingal Bay
note: Bay and beach village with lifeguard-patrolled swimming and the start of the Fingal Island and Shoal Bay tracks (NSW NPWS).

name: Shoal Bay to Fingal Bay Walking Track
note: Walking track between Shoal Bay and Fingal Bay in Tomaree NP (NSW NPWS).

name: Fishermans Bay
note: Foreshore and bay at Nelson Bay with picnic barbecue facilities, named by NPWS.

name: Nelson Bay
note: Town and marina: base for whale and dolphin cruises, dive shops and the Tomaree coast (Wikivoyage Nelson Bay).

name: Anna Bay
note: Town at the foot of Stockton Beach and the sand dunes, with the Birubi dune tours and shark and ray encounters (Wikivoyage Anna Bay).

name: Fly Point
note: Shore dive site at Nelson Bay (with Halifax): macro sea life; a dive site, judged on visitor access.

name: Halifax Park
note: Shore dive site at Nelson Bay (with Fly Point), named by Wikivoyage Nelson Bay.

name: Irukandji Shark & Ray Encounters
note: Shark and ray centre at Anna Bay where visitors swim with sharks and stingrays (paid, daily 9AM-5PM per Wikivoyage); an experience venue.

name: Sand Dune Safaris
note: Operator: sand-dune tours and stand-up sand surfing at Stockton Beach, Anna Bay; operator, not a place.

name: Moonshadow-TQC Cruises
note: Operator: dolphin and whale-watching cruises from Nelson Bay marina; operator, not a place.

name: Imagine Cruises
note: Operator: whale-watching cruises from Nelson Bay; operator, not a place.

name: Port Stephens-Great Lakes Marine Park
note: Marine park: protected waters around Port Stephens and Great Lakes; no visitor-agency page fetched, so it has only Wikipedia support.

name: Surfest
coordinates_source: wikivoyage:Newcastle listing (Merewether Ocean Baths, Merewether Beach)
note: Annual surfing festival at Merewether Beach over 12 days in February. Event, not a permanent spot.

name: Mattara Festival
note: Annual festival at Wallsend Park over the Labour Day weekend. Event, not a permanent spot.

name: This Is Not Art Festival
note: Annual arts festival in Newcastle over the Labour Day long weekend. Event, not a permanent spot.

name: Jazz in the Vines
note: Annual October jazz event hosted by Tyrrell's. Event, not a permanent spot.

name: A Day on the Green
note: Annual concert at Bimbadgen Estate, Pokolbin. Event, not a permanent spot.

name: Central Coast Oyster Festival
note: Annual festival held mid-November on the Central Coast. Event, not a permanent spot.

name: The Entrance Winter Blues & Jazz Festival
note: Annual festival at Memorial Park, The Entrance. Event, not a permanent spot.

name: Spike Fest
note: Annual festival celebrating comedian Spike Milligan (Gosford area). Event, not a permanent spot.
